subsystems.name: Delivery vehicle
subsystems.role: carries the editing payload to the right cells inside the body.

subsystems.name: Editing payload
subsystems.role: the molecular scissors and the address that tells them where to cut.

subsystems.name: Biodistribution and targeting
subsystems.role: determines which organs receive the edit; today mostly the liver.

subsystems.name: Immune management
subsystems.role: controls reactions to the lipid nanoparticle and to Cas9.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing and analytics
subsystems.role: makes and quality-checks the RNA and the formulated particles.

subsystems.name: Clinical administration and monitoring
subsystems.role: delivers the dose and watches for liver and immune effects.

buildSteps.title: Choose the target
buildSteps.detail: Identify the disease-causing gene and pick a guide RNA that cuts next to the mutation with minimal off-target activity.

buildSteps.title: Make the payload
buildSteps.detail: Produce guide RNA and Cas9 mRNA by in vitro transcription, then purify and test them.

buildSteps.title: Formulate lipid nanoparticles
buildSteps.detail: Mix lipids and RNA in a microfluidic device so each particle encloses the payload at a consistent size.

buildSteps.title: Test in animals
buildSteps.detail: Measure editing efficiency, organ distribution and off-target edits in mice and non-human primates.

buildSteps.title: Run safety studies
buildSteps.detail: Toxicology and biodistribution studies support an application to start human trials.

buildSteps.title: Dose escalation in patients
buildSteps.detail: A single intravenous infusion is given, starting at low dose, and the team measures how much the target protein falls.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and adjust
buildSteps.detail: Liver enzymes, immune markers and editing levels are tracked; steroid premedication is used if needed.

buildSteps.title: Follow up long term
buildSteps.detail: Patients are watched for years to confirm the edit lasts and to catch delayed off-target effects.

buildSteps.title: Scale and seek approval
buildSteps.detail: If trials succeed, manufacturing is scaled and regulators review the therapy for market use.

prerequisites.why: the core tool that cuts DNA at a chosen sequence.
Cas9 must be supplied as transient mRNA rather than DNA to limit off-target exposure.
LNPs protect RNA and carry it into cells; they are already used in vaccines.
most LNPs naturally go to the liver; reaching muscle, bone marrow or brain needs new targeting.
many people already have immunity to Cas proteins, which can reduce effectiveness or cause reactions.

pathway.milestone: early-phase trials for liver targets, such as transthyretin amyloidosis, showing large reductions in the disease protein after a single dose
pathway.unlocks: proof that in-vivo editing can work in people.

pathway.milestone: late-stage trials and the first approval for a liver-based genetic disease
pathway.unlocks: a one-time treatment option where patients today need lifelong therapy.

pathway.milestone: delivery systems that reach other organs, including muscle and bone marrow
pathway.unlocks: in-vivo editing for a much wider set of genetic diseases.

pathway.milestone: repeat dosing or redosing becomes safe and reliable
pathway.unlocks: treatment of conditions where a single edit is not enough.
